title: Odile and the Wolf
premise: Yara Delacroix has spent her nineteen years in the Valley of Stillness, where magic cannot enter, serving as the royal food-taster whose body slowly learns to survive every poison. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands and breathes her name like a prophecy, Yara discovers she was born beyond the valley — a child of the old covenant between humans and dragons, smuggled to safety when that pact shattered. Hunted by the king's spymaster and guided by a shapeshifting wolf who is more than he seems, Yara must cross the broken realms and reforge the covenant at the Ember Altar before the last dragon-fire gutters out. In the end she learns the covenant demands a life freely given: she offers her own, but the dragon-mother accepts instead her immunity — every poison she ever survived — leaving Yara mortal, magicless, and finally free, returning home not as a taster of death but as a bridge between worlds.
about_author: Mara Delacroix is the pen name of a former line cook from the Pacific Northwest who swears the best fantasy is written by people who have worked kitchen service. She writes about hunger, loyalty, and the families we cook for.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Yara. A routine tasting goes wrong when a dish meant for the king nearly kills Yara despite her trained immunity — someone is using poison laced with something older than chemistry. The chapter establishes her grim competence, her found family among the castle kitchens, and ends with her coughing silver dust into her palm. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Yara. A burned, half-dead woman collapses at the valley's only gate, clutching a map drawn on dragon-hide. Before dying, she grips Yara's wrist and says, 'It knows your name.' The guards dismiss it; Yara cannot. That night the map's ink moves, tracing a path out of the valley. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a terrible longing for the world outside.

chapters.title: What the Valley Keeps Out
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Yara researches the valley's founding and finds the histories scrubbed clean — except one forbidden folio describing a covenant sealed in fire and a child smuggled inside the wards. The king's spymaster, Corvane, begins asking pointed questions about the dead stranger. Emotional beat: the comfort of home curdling into a cage.

chapters.title: The Wolf at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Fleeing Corvane's arrest, Yara crosses the valley boundary and is ambushed on the far side — saved by an enormous grey wolf who speaks with a man's voice. He calls himself Fen, bound to guard the map's bearer, and is openly disappointed she isn't braver. Emotional beat: terror giving way to reluctant, prickly alliance.

chapters.title: Ash and Rations
chapters.summary: POV Fen. Through the wolf's eyes we see Yara clearly for the first time: stubborn, underfed, secretly cataloguing which plants are safe to eat like the professional survivor she is. They reach the first waypoint — a ruined watchtower — and find evidence others hunt the map. Fen admits he failed the last bearer. Emotional beat: guilt softening into protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Poison Garden
chapters.summary: POV Yara. To cross a borderland choked with toxic flora, Yara does what no one else can: she tastes, tests, and walks them through alive, gaining Fen's genuine respect. But each taste costs her — her immunity is finite, and she feels it thinning. Emotional beat: pride shadowed by the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Corvane's Hounds
chapters.summary: POV Yara. The spymaster's hunters catch up; in the fight, Yara learns Corvane wants the map not for the king but because the covenant's breaking is slowly poisoning the realm itself — the king's madness, the blighted harvests. She also learns Corvane knew her mother. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing everything she thought she fled.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Fen. Sheltering in a village where old rites survive, they meet Maren, a hedge-healer who recognizes the covenant sigil on Yara's skin — a birthmark she always thought was a stain. Maren reveals Yara was dedicated to the dragons before birth. Emotional beat: found family offered, and Yara flinching from it.

chapters.title: Fire in the Deep Road
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Guided underground through the dwarven deep road, the party is trapped when dragon-fire — the last living flame, carried in a lantern by a dying pilgrim — gutters nearby, waking things that should sleep. Yara shields the lantern with her own body and is burned without scarring. Emotional beat: awe; the fire knows her.

chapters.title: Fen's True Shape
chapters.summary: POV Fen. Ambushed at the road's mouth, Fen takes human form to buy Yara time and is gravely wounded — revealing he was once the covenant's sworn knight, cursed to wolf-shape for failing to prevent its breaking. Yara tends him through fever, learning his whole story. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in vulnerability; loyalty vs. truth begins to strain.

chapters.title: The Court of Thorns
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Seeking allies, they petition the fae court of the Thornwood, where Yara must out-negotiate a lady of thorns using nothing but a taster's knowledge of poisons and antidotes. She wins passage and a warning: the Ember Altar demands 'a life freely given,' and the fae know what that means. Emotional beat: triumph laced with foreboding.

chapters.title: Halfway Burned
chapters.summary: POV Fen. Recovering, Fen confesses the full truth: the covenant broke because the last human queen refused to pay its price, and the child smuggled into the valley — Yara — was meant to be raised outside magic so she could choose freely. Yara realizes her whole protected life was someone else's plan. Emotional beat: rage, then grief, then resolve on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: POV Yara. News spreads: the last dragon-fire is failing; the sky over the eastern realms has gone grey, crops dying, magic unraveling. Refugees clog the roads. Yara sees what the covenant's death means for ordinary people — the same kind of people she fed and guarded in the castle. Emotional beat: responsibility shifting from personal to universal.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Corvane corners them, offering alliance: he'll get them to the Altar if Yara lets him control the new covenant's terms — binding dragons to human law forever. His motive is revealed as love for the mad king and guilt over Yara's mother, whom he failed. Emotional beat: sympathy for the antagonist; Yara refuses to let fear write the terms again.

chapters.title: The Dragon-Mother's Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Fen. They climb to the roost of Vessarath, the dragon-mother, ancient and half-asleep, sustained by the guttering flame. She tests Yara not with riddles but with memory — showing her the mother who gave her away, the queen who refused to pay, the whole wound of the broken pact. Emotional beat: devastating compassion; understanding replaces blame.

chapters.title: Terms of Fire
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Vessarath names the price: a life freely given at the Ember Altar, or the fire dies and the realms with it. Fen offers himself to repay his ancient failure; Yara refuses to let him. Corvane arrives with armies at the mountain's foot, ready to seize the Altar by force if negotiation fails. Emotional beat: love weaponized against self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Battle Below the Altar
chapters.summary: POV Fen. Corvane's soldiers clash with fae and village levies on the mountain slopes while Yara climbs toward the Altar. Fen, torn between guarding her and stopping the slaughter, chooses to break his curse-bound obedience — and in choosing, the curse cracks. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth resolved in action; freedom bought by defiance.

chapters.title: The Ember Altar
chapters.summary: POV Yara. At the Altar, Yara understands the covenant was never meant to take a life — the queens misread it for generations. It asks for what sustains life: hers is her hard-won immunity, every poison survived, the very thing that defined her. She gives it willingly. The fire roars back. Emotional beat: transcendence; identity surrendered and transformed.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Reborn covenant, but changed: Yara can now be poisoned, hurt, killed — mortal in every way. Vessarath names her Covenant-Bearer, a bridge between realms, and Fen, curse broken, stands before her as a man for the first time. Corvane, defeated and grieving, kneels. Emotional beat: hollow triumph turning toward peace.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Yara returns to the valley, now open to the world, and faces the king — healed of madness as the land heals — and the kitchen family who never stopped setting a place for her. She can no longer taste-test, but she teaches the next generation of tasters to read danger differently. Emotional beat: belonging redefined; found family restored.

chapters.title: The Bridge Between
chapters.summary: POV Fen. One year later: trade caravans cross the old boundaries, dragons fly openly, and Fen — knight no longer, wolf no longer — builds a life beside Yara at the valley gate where they met. A young girl arrives carrying a moving map, and Yara smiles, knowing exactly what to do. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the cycle continued by choice, not fate.

chapters.title: Odile and the Wolf
chapters.summary: POV Yara, epilogue. Years on, Yara tells the story of the dying stranger, the wolf, and the fire to children of two realms gathered at the Altar's light — including the truth that survival is not the same as living, and that the dearest price is the one paid gladly. The last image: dragon-fire reflected in a shared meal. Emotional beat: warmth, legacy, closure.
